Subject: Migrating inter-service communication from REST to gRPC

---

Hi team,

**We're moving forward with gRPC for all inter-service communication, starting next sprint.** Here's the full context so you can act on this without needing a sync.

---

**The decision**

After evaluating our current REST setup against two alternatives — gRPC and GraphQL — we're adopting gRPC as our inter-service transport layer.

---

**Why not GraphQL?**

GraphQL was a serious contender, primarily because of its flexible querying and strong tooling for client-driven data fetching. We ruled it out for inter-service use for two reasons:

1. **It's optimized for the wrong boundary.** GraphQL shines at the client-to-server edge where query shape flexibility matters. Between internal services, we control both ends of every call — that flexibility becomes overhead, not value.
2. **Operational complexity.** Schema stitching and federation add maintenance burden we'd be taking on without a clear payoff in our architecture.

---

**Why not stay on REST?**

REST works, and switching has real costs. We're making the move because our profiling data ([see the latency dashboard](https://link-to-dashboard)) showed consistent serialization overhead and schema drift across service boundaries that REST's loose contracts don't prevent. The pain is real and growing.

---

**Why gRPC?**

- Protobuf contracts enforce schema consistency at compile time, eliminating the drift problem
- Measurable serialization performance improvement (benchmarks in the [spike doc](https://link-to-spike-doc))
- Bidirectional streaming unblocks two roadmap items we've been deferring

**What we're giving up:** gRPC is harder to debug than REST — no curl-friendly requests, and browser support requires a proxy layer. We're accepting that tradeoff. Tooling like [grpcurl](https://github.com/fullstorydev/grpcurl) and [gRPC-web](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web) mitigates it, but it's not zero cost.

---

**What this means for you**

The migration plan and service prioritization are in the [RFC doc](https://link-to-rfc). Please read it before next sprint planning — it covers rollout order, the Protobuf style guide we're adopting, and the timeline for deprecating existing REST endpoints.

If you have concerns about the decision itself, reply here by **[date]** so we can address them before work begins. Once we're past that date, the decision is locked and feedback should move to implementation details.

---

Rachel

Subject: Migrating inter-service communication from REST to gRPC

---

Hi team,

**We're moving forward with gRPC for all inter-service communication, starting next sprint.** Here's the full context so you can act on this without needing a sync.

---

**The decision**

After evaluating our current REST setup against two alternatives — gRPC and GraphQL — we're adopting gRPC as our inter-service transport layer.

---

**Why not GraphQL?**

GraphQL was a serious contender, primarily because of its flexible querying and strong tooling for client-driven data fetching. We ruled it out for inter-service use for two reasons:

1. **It's optimized for the wrong boundary.** GraphQL shines at the client-to-server edge where query shape flexibility matters. Between internal services, we control both ends of every call — that flexibility becomes overhead, not value.
2. **Operational complexity.** Schema stitching and federation add maintenance burden we'd be taking on without a clear payoff in our architecture.

---

**Why not stay on REST?**

REST works, and switching has real costs. We're making the move because our profiling data ([latency dashboard](https://link-to-dashboard)) showed consistent serialization overhead and schema drift across service boundaries that REST's loose contracts don't prevent. The pain is real and growing.

---

**Why gRPC?**

- Protobuf contracts enforce schema consistency at compile time, eliminating the drift problem
- Measurable serialization performance improvement ([spike doc §3](https://link-to-spike-doc) has the benchmarks)
- Bidirectional streaming unblocks two roadmap items we've been deferring

**What we're giving up:** gRPC is harder to debug than REST — no curl-friendly requests, and browser support requires a proxy layer. We're accepting that tradeoff. [grpcurl](https://github.com/fullstorydev/grpcurl) and [gRPC-web](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web) mitigate it, but it's not zero cost.

---

**What this means for you**

Rollout order, the Protobuf style guide, and the REST endpoint deprecation timeline are all in the [RFC](https://link-to-rfc). Please read it before sprint planning.

---

If you have concerns about this decision, please reply to this thread by **[date]** with feedback in one of these areas:

- **Architectural concerns** — something about our service topology that makes gRPC a poor fit we haven't accounted for
- **Security implications** — TLS configuration, mTLS requirements, or anything in our threat model that needs addressing before rollout
- **Team capacity** — if your service is sequenced in a way that conflicts with other commitments already on the board

What's not in scope for this round: implementation details, Protobuf naming conventions, or toolchain preferences. Those belong in the RFC comments, not here.

Once we're past **[date]**, the decision is locked and further feedback should move to the RFC.

---

Rachel

Subject: Migrating inter-service communication from REST to gRPC

---

Hi team,

**We're moving forward with gRPC for all inter-service communication, starting next sprint.** Here's the full context so you can act on this without needing a sync.

---

**The decision**

After evaluating our current REST setup against two alternatives — gRPC and GraphQL — we're adopting gRPC as our inter-service transport layer.

---

**Why not GraphQL?**

GraphQL was a serious contender, primarily because of its flexible querying and strong tooling for client-driven data fetching. We ruled it out for inter-service use for two reasons:

1. **It's optimized for the wrong boundary.** GraphQL shines at the client-to-server edge where query shape flexibility matters. Between internal services, we control both ends of every call — that flexibility becomes overhead, not value.
2. **Operational complexity.** Schema stitching and federation add maintenance burden we'd be taking on without a clear payoff in our architecture.

---

**Why not stay on REST?**

REST works, and switching has real costs. We're making the move because our profiling data ([latency dashboard](https://link-to-dashboard)) showed consistent serialization overhead and schema drift across service boundaries that REST's loose contracts don't prevent. The pain is real and growing.

---

**Why gRPC?**

- Protobuf contracts enforce schema consistency at compile time, eliminating the drift problem
- Measurable serialization performance improvement ([spike doc §3](https://link-to-spike-doc) has the benchmarks)
- Bidirectional streaming unblocks two roadmap items we've been deferring

**What we're giving up:** gRPC is harder to debug than REST — no curl-friendly requests, and browser support requires a proxy layer. We're accepting that tradeoff. [grpcurl](https://github.com/fullstorydev/grpcurl) and [gRPC-web](https://github.com/grpc/grpc-web) mitigate it, but it's not zero cost.

---

**What this means for you**

Rollout order, the Protobuf style guide, and the REST endpoint deprecation timeline are all in the [RFC](https://link-to-rfc). Please read it before sprint planning.

If this email surfaces a separate topic — team resourcing, REST deprecation scheduling, Protobuf toolchain setup — please start a new thread rather than replying here. This thread is scoped to the migration decision itself.

---

**One ask before next sprint planning**

If you have concerns about this decision, please reply to this thread by **[date]** with feedback in one of these areas:

- **Architectural concerns** — something about our service topology that makes gRPC a poor fit we haven't accounted for
- **Security implications** — TLS configuration, mTLS requirements, or anything in our threat model that needs addressing before rollout
- **Team capacity** — if your service is sequenced in a way that conflicts with other commitments already on the board

What's not in scope for this round: implementation details, Protobuf naming conventions, or toolchain preferences. Those belong in the RFC comments, not here.

Once we're past **[date]**, the decision is locked and further feedback should move to the RFC.

---

Rachel
